$comment: Known-unfixable production advisories. The audit gate (scripts/audit-gate.mjs)
fails on ANY high/critical advisory that is NOT listed here, so a NEWLY
introduced vulnerability still blocks the merge. Entries are keyed by GHSA id,
never by package name, so a FUTURE different advisory in the same package is
- Every entry MUST have a reason and a reviewBy date (YYYY-MM-DD).
- An entry past its reviewBy date FAILS the gate. That is intentional: it
forces a re-check instead of a silent permanent exception.
- Remove an entry as soon as an upstream fix ships. The gate warns when an
entry no longer matches anything (stale) so it gets cleaned up.
- Adding an entry is a security decision and needs review, like any other

allow.reason: Fix requires sharp >=0.35.0, but next pins sharp@^0.34.3, so bumping only apps/api creates a DUPLICATE sharp (0.35.x nested + 0.34.5 hoisted) and leaves the vulnerable copy in the tree. A forced root override is required and sharp is the package behind past deploy failures, so it needs its own PR with a build test.
allow.trackedBy: resolved by the next 15->16 upgrade (next 16 allows sharp 0.35) or a reviewed root override
